title: HB 205 (2021 Regular Session): AN ACT relating to voting.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085(1)(e)[(d)])
(quote) if the voter provides proof of identification as defined in KRS 117.375 or meets the requirements of KRS 117.228 and 117.229, and the voter:
(b_no_id_remedy)
(note) undefined
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085(1)(a)2.)
(quote) In lieu of requesting an application for a mail-in absentee ballot, a voter may apply for a mail-in absentee ballot through a secure online portal established by the State Board of Elections in administrative regulations promulgated under KRS Chapter 13A. The secure online portal shall have the capacity to ensure verification of the identity of the voter through an identity document, as defined in KRS 186.010, on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet.
(section) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085(1)(a)2.)
(quote) If a voter does not have an identity document on file with the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, the voter may confirm his or her identity as required under KRS 117.227 by completing the voter's affirmation required under KRS 117.228 and provided on the secure online portal.
(section) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085(2)(c))
(quote) Returned to the county clerk either by mail or in-person with[and the voter shall provide] a copy of the voter's[his or her] proof of identification, as defined in KRS 117.375, or the executed voter affirmation as described in KRS 117.228(1)(c).
(section) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085(6))
(quote) The county clerk shall retain the voter's mail-in ballot application form, which shall include the photographed copy of the voter's proof of identification or the voter affirmation as prescribed by KRS 117.228(1)(c), and the postal form or Intelligent Mail barcode required by subsection (3) of this section for twenty-two (22) months after the primary or election.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) Sec. 1 (KRS 117.085): adds the online portal as an alternative to requesting a paper application; lets county clerks track mail-in ballots with Intelligent Mail barcodes; sets steps for a voter who requested but did not receive a mail-in ballot, or who wants to vote in person after getting one (signed affirmation, ballot cancelled); covered voters who cannot return a mail-in ballot sign the affirmation at the polls.
(other) Sec. 2: KRS 14.312 - address-confidentiality program participants may vote by mail-in ballot; cross-reference to 117.085 updated.
(other) Sec. 3: KRS 117.165 - county board examines voting machines before the election; cross-reference to 117.085 updated.
(other) Sec. 4: KRS 117.235 - who may be in the voting room; conforming change only (text read does not touch ID).
(other) version: orig_bill (the only version): introduced text; slot c (portal ID check; ID copy or affirmation with the application) and the unchanged in-person absentee ID cross-reference in slot a. No other versions saved.
(other) note: Introduced only; sent to Committee on Committees and no further action. Bracketed words are deleted. The requirement to send a copy of proof of identification, or the executed affirmation, with a mail-in application is reprinted with rewording ('and the voter shall provide' struck, 'with' added); because no unbracketed side-by-side of current law is in the files, I cannot say from the text alone that the ID-or-affirmation rule itself is new, and its wording suggests it already existed. The new part is the portal route: Transportation Cabinet identity-document check, else the affirmation. 'Proof of identification as defined in KRS 117.375' is not defined in this bill. The in-person absentee ID words in slot a are unbracketed, so I read them as reprinted law.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
